briefing.headline: Agents and brokers consolidate as AI reshapes risk
briefing.teaser: Small agency deals, AI in claims calls, and new cover for AI-driven risk
briefing.whatsHappening: The newest stories show AI moving from pilot to daily operations: one carrier now lets AI handle most first-notice-of-loss calls, and a cargo cover can be quoted straight through ChatGPT. At the same time AI is being treated as a source of risk, with AXA's survey ranking it above climate change as experts' top concern and cyber claims shifting as AI failures create new liability. Deal-making is mixed: small agency purchases like King Risk Partners adding two Florida firms continue, even as agency M&A is reported at an eight-year low with private-equity exits looming. Partnerships round out the picture, from Aviva and insureMO taking embedded insurance across Europe to Shory teaming up with the UAE's cyber council.
briefing.whyItMatters: As AI takes over front-line tasks, insurers will have to decide who is accountable when an automated decision goes wrong, which is the question behind the cyber-liability shift. A slowdown in agency deals alongside looming PE exits could change who owns the brokers and agencies carriers rely on. Watch whether the thin pace of agency M&A picks up, and whether AI-specific cover keeps appearing as fast as AI-specific exposure.
